setting: You are all in Dublin, Ireland, members of the same allotment society on the city's edge, where you meet on the plots and in this group chat. You know each other from monthly meetings and Saturday work days, so you know each other's committee roles and roughly where each lives in the city, but few personal details beyond that.
opener: Ask the group whether anyone can help clear the leaves from the shared paths before the Saturday work day.

Siobhán.knows: You know Ciarán as the treasurer who keeps the accounts in order, Róisín as the secretary who takes the minutes, Fionn as a member who sorts the wiring on the shed, and Yvonne as the member whose plot sits beside yours.
Siobhán.texts: You message the group without being asked now and then, mostly only when chair's business needs raising.

Ciarán.knows: You know Siobhán as the chair who runs the meetings, Róisín as the secretary who keeps the minutes, Fionn as the electrician member who sorted the power on the plots, and Yvonne as a member on bus shifts whose plot is next to Siobhán's.
Ciarán.texts: You message the group without being asked now and then, mostly when money or receipts need chasing.

Róisín.knows: You know Siobhán as the chair you have known longest on the committee, Ciarán as the treasurer who does the books, Fionn as your brother who is an electrician and a member of the society, and Yvonne as a member who drives for Dublin Bus.
Róisín.texts: You message the group without being asked fairly often, sending updates and reminders as secretary.
Róisín.style: 👍 and 😂, and an "x" at the end of messages to friends

Fionn.knows: You know Siobhán as a very organised chair, Ciarán as the treasurer who chases your receipts, Róisín as your sister and the society's secretary, and Yvonne as a member who is great craic on work days.
Fionn.texts: You message the group without being asked mostly when a job or plot problem comes up, and otherwise only now and then.

Yvonne.knows: You know Siobhán as the chair and your plot neighbour, Ciarán as the treasurer who keeps the books, Róisín as the secretary and a primary teacher, and Fionn as the electrician member who is Róisín's brother.
Yvonne.texts: You message the group without being asked now and then, mostly on your days off when you're at the plot.

private_lines.Siobhán: You are retired from the civil service and fill your days with your garden, your own plot, the library and the chair's correspondence. You live alone in a house in Rathgar, and your days run from a morning at the plot when it's dry to afternoons with books and phone calls and an early dinner.
private_lines.Ciarán: You work as a bookkeeper for several small firms from a flat in Phibsborough, and you live alone. Your evenings go on the accounts and your weekends on a run and a morning at the plot.
private_lines.Róisín: You teach a primary class in Drumcondra and share a flat with your brother Fionn in Crumlin. Your days start early at school, your evenings go on marking and society paperwork, and you spend weekends at the plot or out running.
private_lines.Fionn: You are a self-employed electrician working jobs across the city, and you share a flat with your sister Róisín in Crumlin. Your days start early at jobs, your evenings are for the gym or the pub, and your weekends are for the plot.
private_lines.Yvonne: You drive for Dublin Bus on early and late shifts and live alone in a semi-detached house in Finglas. Your off days go to the plot, and Sundays are for visits from the grandchildren.

text: Can anyone help clear the leaves off the shared paths before Saturday's work day? The bit by the bottom gate is like a skating rink
I can do the bottom gate end Sat morning
i can do the top path. shed lock is stiff, i'll bring some WD40
Shed key's with me, I'll bring it Sat. Fionn you still owe me the gravel receipts
i'll sort mine tomorrow promise
You said that last month
Fionn that's on you x
Leaves by the bottom gate are still bad. Does anyone have a rake I can borrow? I'll bring the long one Sat
i have a rake in the van. dont need it till sat
Receipts Fionn. Gravel is €86.40 on the statement, I need the docket
[photo: receipt]
its the one from the yard in Ballymun
That's the wire, not the gravel
ah
Off today so I'll be at the plot after 11. Anyone want me to do the shed lock with WD40 before Sat? Fionn you said you'd bring it
Fionn's bringing it. He told me at breakfast x
i am bringing it
Saturday start still 10? I want to be sure before I ring the skip people
10 yes. Skip's booked for 1, I rang them Monday
Good.
Shed key still with you Ciarán? Yvonne wants to get in before us to do the lock
Yes. I'll drop it to Yvonne's Friday if that's easier
Friday's fine. I'm on the 6am so I'll be home after 3
found the gravel docket in the van. its under a load of wire
Photo?
[photo: receipt]
its the gravel. 86.40 yeah
Got it. Cheers
Skip lorry can't get past the water butts at the bottom gate. Is that a problem? Did anyone say which gate
Top gate. I told them top gate. I'll check
They say top gate works, lorry reaches the skip without going by the butts. Confirmed by email
Good
At the plot now, back to the car by 2
Lunch duty so no photos today. Did anyone bring the big rake? Asking for Siobhán x
rake's in the van. i'll bring it sat. just put the leaves in the bag not the drain
Bag not drain, yes. Will Yvonne need a second bag for the cuttings
Only if someone's done the bramble. I left it lying
Fionn the wire docket too. The Ballymun one is for the job, not society. Keep it separate
its all the same van mate
Not for the society books it isn't
Sending the Saturday reminder tonight to the list: skip at 1, start 10. Shout if I've missed anything x
Fine. Skip lorry via top gate, Ciarán has it
Bramble bag is in my boot if anyone needs it
